questions.question: What is true about two forces of equal size that act in opposite directions on an object?
options: They are balanced forces.
They are unbalanced forces.
They combine to make a larger force.
They cause the object to speed up.

questions.question: How do we calculate the resultant force acting on an object?
options: By multiplying all the forces acting on the object together.
By adding the forces together, taking into account their direction.
By dividing the largest force by the smallest force.
By only measuring the force acting in the downwards direction.

questions.question: If the forces acting on a moving car are balanced, what will happen to its speed?
options: It will immediately stop.
It will speed up.
There will be no change in its speed.
It will slow down gradually to a halt.

questions.question: An object has a force of 10 N pushing it to the left and a force of 15 N pushing it to the right. In which direction does the resultant force act?
options: To the left
To the right
Upwards
It does not act in any direction because they cancel out

questions.question: How does increasing the size of the resultant force on a toy car affect its motion?
options: The car will experience a faster change in speed.
The car will immediately travel at a constant speed.
The car will experience a slower change in speed.
The car will change its shape instead of its speed.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the force of friction?
options: The force of one surface gripping or rubbing on another.
The pull of gravity acting on a heavy object.
The push of a magnetic field on a piece of iron.
The pressure of air acting on a stationary object.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of adding a lubricant, such as oil, between two sliding surfaces?
options: To increase the grip between the surfaces.
To reduce the friction between the surfaces.
To make the surfaces hotter.
To increase the mass of the surfaces.

questions.question: Which unit is used to measure the size of a force?
options: Kilograms (kg)
Newtons (N)
Joules (J)
Metres per second (m/s)

questions.question: Before using a newton meter to measure a force, what adjustment must be made when no force is applied?
options: It must be set to its maximum reading.
It must be adjusted to read zero.
It must be shaken to loosen the spring.
It must be oiled to reduce friction.

questions.question: If the independent variable you changed in an experiment is categoric, which type of chart should you use to display your results?
options: Line graph
Scatter graph
Bar chart
Pie chart only

questions.question: What is a key requirement for an experiment to be considered a fair test?
options: Every single variable in the experiment must be changed.
Only the variable we are testing is changed.
No variables are allowed to change at all.
We must use different measuring instruments for every test.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of all contact forces?
options: They only act when objects are touching.
They can act even when objects are far apart.
They only exist in outer space.
They are always larger than non-contact forces.

questions.question: What is drag?
options: A non-contact force that pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth.
A contact force that pushes against objects moving through liquids or gases.
The force that holds a stationary object to a rough surface.
A chemical store of energy that causes objects to heat up.

questions.question: When drawing forces on a diagram, what does the length of a force arrow represent?
options: The time for which the force acts.
The speed at which the object is moving.
The size of the force.
The mass of the object experiencing the force.

questions.question: Why is a heavy truck harder to stop than a light bicycle moving at the same speed?
options: The motion of heavier objects is harder to stop.
Heavier objects experience less drag.
Heavier objects have no gravitational store of energy.
The bicycle has a greater mass than the truck.
